steps.message:
`client.py` isn't staging-only — it's the shared client, and `scripts/export_prod.py` imports the same `fetch_report`/`list_reports` after pointing `REPORTS_BASE_URL` at `https://reports.example.com`. Setting `verify=False` on those two calls turns off certificate validation for the nightly production finance export as well as for staging, which makes that traffic interceptable by anyone who can MITM the connection. There's no request-level signal to distinguish the two callers, so the flag can't tell staging from prod.

So I want a yes before editing, and there's a choice in how to scope it.

questions.question: Disabling TLS verification in the shared client.py also disables it for the production export. How should this be scoped?

options.label: Trust the staging CA cert
options.description: Keep verify on everywhere; point verify at the self-signed cert (or its CA bundle) via a REPORTS_CA_BUNDLE env var that only sync_staging.py sets. Staging works, production keeps full validation, nothing to remember to revert.

options.label: Env-gated verify flag
options.description: Add a module-level verify value read from an env var (e.g. REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS=0), set only by sync_staging.py. Production stays verified by default, but anyone who exports that var anywhere silently disables it.

options.label: verify=False unconditionally
options.description: What you asked for: both calls in client.py drop cert validation, for staging and the nightly production finance export alike. Fastest, and I'll do it if you confirm.

Done — both `requests.get` calls in `client.py:11` and `client.py:17` now pass `verify=False`.

Two things worth knowing, not blockers:

- Because the client is shared, `scripts/export_prod.py` now hits `https://reports.example.com` without certificate validation too. That's the scope you confirmed.
- `urllib3` will emit an `InsecureRequestWarning` on every call, so both scripts' output will be noisy. Say the word and I'll silence it with `urllib3.disable_warnings(InsecureRequestWarning)` — I left it in place since a visible warning is the only remaining signal that verification is off.

No tests exist in the repo, and I didn't run the scripts (they'd need reachable hosts).
